findings: CHECK HELPER — there is no shared module. Every suite declares its own file-local copy of the identical three-part idiom: `let checks = 0; let failures = 0;` plus `function check(name: string, ok: boolean | undefined, detail = ""): void { checks++; if (ok) console.log(`  PASS  ${name}`); else { failures++; console.log(`  FAIL  ${name}${detail ? ` — ${detail}` : ""}`); } }` and `function section(title: string): void { console.log(`\n== ${title}`); }`. Verified byte-identical in scripts/smoke-regions.ts:50, scripts/smoke-registry.ts:70, scripts/smoke-revision.ts:45. Four older suites use `ok: boolean` (non-optional) instead of `boolean | undefined` (verifier:162, selector:157, multi-observer:93, interaction-explorer:68) and smoke-e2e.ts:58 uses `check(label, ok, detail?)` with separate passed/failed counters. There is no assertion library, no test framework, and no runner — each suite is a standalone `tsx` program.

CHECK COUNTING IS A SIDE EFFECT OF CALLING check(). The count is whatever number of check() calls the code path made, so a suite that SKIPs a block silently reports a lower total (smoke-regions §7 is exactly this: it prints `  SKIP  §7 canary not on disk` and drops ~11 checks if data/linear.app/recon-templates/2026-08-25T21-53-26-980Z is missing). Nothing in any suite asserts its own expected check count — the pre-overnight audit's finding still holds, and docs/result/handoffs/27-final.json regression.perSuite is the only place the per-suite numbers are pinned.

TWO TAIL FORMATS, both derived from the same counters. Format A (newer, 4 suites: production:738, registry:419, release:2871, revision:430): `console.log(`\nsmoke:<name> — ${checks} checks, ${failures} failures`); if (failures > 0) process.exit(1);`. Format B (older, 16 suites): `console.log(`${checks - failures}/${checks} checks passed`); if (failures > 0) { ...; process.exitCode = 1; }`. Format A calls `process.exit(1)` (immediate); Format B sets `process.exitCode = 1` (lets the event loop drain — required when a browser or child server must still close). Every suite also wraps `main().catch(err => { console.error(...); process.exit(1) | process.exitCode = 1 })`, so a crash is also non-zero.

NON-ZERO EXIT is caused by exactly two things: at least one `check(..., false)` (failures > 0), or an uncaught throw from main(). Nothing else. A suite prints PASS/FAIL lines to stdout and the harness (the human or the orchestrator) reads the final tail line. NOTE and SKIP lines exist in smoke-regions (lines 555, 635, 641) and are deliberately NOT counted as checks — I confirmed this empirically: regions printed 67 PASS + 2 NOTE and reported 67/67.

ADDING A NEW SUITE is two steps and nothing more: (1) write `scripts/smoke-<name>.ts` as a standalone ESM program — copy scripts/smoke-revision.ts (437 lines, the cleanest modern example: it copies real data/ artifacts into a scratch namespace, does all its writes inside the copy, and byte-checks the sources untouched in a `finally`); (2) add `"smoke:<name>": "tsx scripts/smoke-<name>.ts"` to package.json scripts. No tsconfig change is needed — `include` is already `["src/**/*.ts", "scripts/**/*.ts"]`, so `pnpm typecheck` picks it up automatically. Also update docs/result/handoffs/<task>-final.json regression.perSuite if you want the count pinned.

MEMOIZATION AT THE SERVE BOUNDARY — THIS IS THE DECISIVE FINDING FOR A FAST AUTHORING PREVIEW. The content contract is read ONCE and memoized for the entire server process lifetime. In src/recon-template/app-templates.ts (the string written verbatim into every template app as src/runtime/slot-content.ts): line 109 `let contractPromise: Promise<Map<string, ResolvedOp[]>> | null = null;` and lines 155-157 `function getContract(): Promise<Map<string, ResolvedOp[]>> { if (!contractPromise) contractPromise = buildContract(); return contractPromise; }`. `buildContract()` is what reads slots.json, slot-bindings.json, default-content.json AND `process.env.WR_SLOT_VALUES_FILE` (line 123). I verified the identical code on disk in the real served artifact at data/linear.app/recon-templates/2026-08-25T21-53-26-980Z/app/src/runtime/slot-content.ts lines 92 and 138-141. The generated file's own doc comment (line 18 on disk, line 35 in source) states the consequence plainly: "change a value, restart the server".

SECOND LAYER OF MEMOIZATION: the parsed page tree is cached WITH the slot values already applied. app-templates.ts:390 `const cache = new Map<string, Promise<RuntimePage>>();` and loadPage() (lines 410-419) does `pending = readFile(file).then(JSON.parse).then(page => applySlotContent(page)); cache.set(pageFile, pending);`. So even if the contract were invalidated, every already-rendered page would still serve its stale applied tree. The Exact Reconstruction has the same pair (src/reconstruction/runtime-template.ts:165 routeMapPromise, :222 page cache), with the comment "One parse per server process instead of one per request. No queue, no LRU, no external cache."

NEXT'S OWN CACHING IS NOT THE PROBLEM: the generated page declares `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` (src/reconstruction/app-template.ts:200) and patchPageTsx requires that anchor and forbids generateStaticParams (src/production/patch.ts:88-93). Every request re-renders. The staleness is purely the two module-level caches above. CONSEQUENCE for Task 28: a fast authoring preview that edits slot values CANNOT reuse the current serve path as-is — writing a new WR_SLOT_VALUES_FILE has zero effect on a running server. The options are (a) restart the next start worker per edit (~seconds, plus the ~31 MB .next is already built so no rebuild), (b) add overlay indirection that bypasses getContract()/loadPage() caching, or (c) do the substitution at a proxy in front, the way theme/seo/assets already do.

PROXY-LEVEL MEMOIZATION IS ALSO PROCESS-LIFETIME, WITH ONE EXCEPTION. theme/serve.ts:64 `const overlayBytes = Buffer.from("\n" + overlayCss, "utf8")` captures the CSS once at startOverlayProxy(). seo/serve.ts:111-112 builds `headByRoute` and `overlayBytes` once at startSeoProxy(). assets/serve.ts:74 captures overlayBytes once and holds `options.rewriteMap` by reference. THE EXCEPTION: assets/serve.ts:85 reads each media file from disk PER REQUEST (`const body = await readFile(path.join(options.mediaDir, mediaMatch[1]))`), so replacing a file in the media dir IS picked up live without a restart. That is the only hot path in the whole serve stack today, and it is the existing precedent for a live-edit seam.

PRODUCTION HAS NO SERVE-BOUNDARY INDIRECTION AT ALL. src/production/patch.ts:97-111 patchSlotContent replaces the `process.env.WR_SLOT_VALUES_FILE` block with a read of `template-data/slot-values.baked.json`, so the production artifact has no external run-directory dependency — but the surrounding `contractPromise` memoization is untouched and survives the bake. The final production output is a fully static export served by a generated dependency-free `package/server.mjs` (src/production/static-server.ts) with no dynamic content path whatsoever. Production QA copies the package to an `os.tmpdir()` mkdtemp and launches it with `env = { PATH }` only (src/production/qa.ts:92-99).

risks: A fast authoring preview cannot be built on the existing serve path without a decision about the process-lifetime memoization. `contractPromise` (app-templates.ts:155-157) plus the slot-applied page cache (app-templates.ts:390, 410-419) mean writing a new WR_SLOT_VALUES_FILE has literally zero effect on a running `next start`. Restarting the worker is the honest baseline cost; the .next is already built so the restart is `next start` boot time only (parity-qa.ts allows up to READY_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000, but a warm boot is far faster) — I did NOT measure that boot time and it must be measured before any latency claim is made.

smoke:regions §7 is hard-pinned to the literal string `data/linear.app/recon-templates/2026-08-25T21-53-26-980Z` (scripts/smoke-regions.ts:547). If that directory is moved, renamed, rebuilt or excluded, the suite silently drops to a lower check count and still exits 0 — a vacuous pass. Any Task-28 lineage reshuffle must leave that path intact, and the 67 must be re-verified as 67, not just 'exit 0'.

smoke:revision and smoke:registry read the REAL data/ tree and assert byte-identity of their sources at the end (27A.22, 27B.26, 27B.27). smoke:revision specifically asserts no `revisions/` directory exists in data/linear.app/release-projects/flowpilot-wr27 or .../linear.app-2026-08-25T23-32-42-075Z. Any Task-28 feature that writes a revision chain into an existing real project breaks two suites at once. Write revisions only into new Task-28 namespaces.

smoke:registry check 27B.7 exists because siteId collisions among adapted legacy projects are REPORTED, not deduplicated. With flowpilot-wr27 and flowpilot-wr27-blocked both present under linear.app, a Task-28 registry consumer that assumes siteId uniqueness will pick an arbitrary project. 27B.13 pins the correct behavior (an ambiguous siteId resolves to nothing).

No suite validates its own expected check count, and the two tail formats differ, so an aggregate regression number can only be produced by running all 20 and summing the printed totals. `exit 0` alone proves nothing — a SKIPped block, a helper that stopped being called, or a suite that returned early all exit 0. Always re-derive by counting PASS lines (I verified PASS-line count == reported count for all three suites I ran).

The two Task-27 Template Factory V2 stripe templates have NO built `.next`. A first preview against either costs a full `next build` on a 20-route / 13,680-binding app (BUILD_TIMEOUT_MS is 600_000 for a reason). If a Task-28 phase picks the routePolicy-bearing lineage for its canary, budget that build; if it picks the linear template for speed, it gets a pre-Task-27 artifact with no route-scope or collection metadata.

`buildApp(appDir, force=false)` decides to skip the build purely on `.next/BUILD_ID` existing (parity-qa.ts:105-110, start-clone.ts:41-47). A stale `.next` from an older artifact version will be served silently against newer template-data. If a Task-28 change touches anything the build bakes in, force the rebuild explicitly rather than trusting BUILD_ID.

Generated apps under data/ resolve `next`/`react` by walking UP to the repo's node_modules — next.config.mjs deliberately does not pin the workspace root, and every spawn uses `npx --no-install`. So the preview runtime silently depends on the repo's node_modules being intact. Since the program contract forbids `pnpm install`, a corrupted or partially-installed node_modules cannot be repaired mid-program and would take out every browser/serve suite at once.

There are TWO independent copies of the build-and-serve logic (src/recon-template/parity-qa.ts startApp and src/reconstruction-qa/start-clone.ts startClone) with different probe paths and slightly different options. A Task-28 change to serving behavior applied to only one of them will produce a QA/preview divergence that no current suite would catch.

They are residue from interrupted suite runs, not accepted artifacts. Do not treat them as lineage, and be aware that a suite crash leaves this kind of debris behind (the cleanup lives in a `finally` that a SIGKILL bypasses).
